extracted.intended_audience: Unemployment Insurance Commission (UIC) claims adjudication staff (Agents I and II), unit supervisors, and other UIC officers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria for processing, examining, deciding, and referring unemployment insurance benefit applications within UIC units, including division of responsibilities between Agents I and II and interaction with Canada Manpower Centres (CMCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal determination based on prior benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a new claim is a renewal of a prior application by obtaining a complete listing of the date and length of previous benefits and checking whether the new claim occurs within a certain period following the establishment of a previous claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions made fairly recently as a result of a previous application may still affect the outcome of the new application; clerk notes results of this control procedure on a slip for the benefit of the deciding Agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documentation to open a file
rubrics_metrics.description: Open a file under the claimant's social insurance number containing the completed and signed application for benefit, Record of Employment (if available), medical certificate for sickness or maternity claims, CMC registration form, claimant's statement of rights and obligations, file on previous applications within the past year, slip indicating state of any prior application, and a control slip for internal statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents constitute the basic documentation required for the officer to make a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process applications without delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Process the application promptly in accordance with sec. 53(3) and 54(2) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a claim is presented in person, decision should be made if possible on the spot and the claimant notified immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatcher assignment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When application submitted in person, dispatcher records name and social insurance number; the last digit indicates the service unit to which the claim should be assigned and the dispatcher introduces the claimant to the available agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application arrives by mail, it is forwarded after data control to the appropriate unit and distributed by the unit supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of decision-making authority between Agents I and II
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-making authority is delegated to two classes: basic responsibility vested in Agents II with subsidiary responsibility to Agents I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents II normally handle applications assigned to their unit; Agents I are authorized to decide a variety of more straightforward cases to relieve Agents II of workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell working relationship and responsibility principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Agent I works closely in a cell with an Agent II; although Agent II is higher classified there is no chain of command within the cell; whoever is responsible for a claim file makes his decision on his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent I receives instruction to consult more experienced colleague on doubtful points; quality control is exercised by the Supervisor of insurance services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentious vs non-contentious distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC distinguishes between 'contentious' and 'non-contentious' matters; only non-contentious matters may be decided by an Agent I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction is based on degree of difficulty and probability the case will later result in litigation rather than literal litigation at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I duty to forward when case appears contentious
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on examining the file or after contact with the claimant, the Agent I decides the application raises matters he is not authorized to decide, he must forward the file to an Agent II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files that become more complicated during interview must also be passed on when new elements arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I authority: existence of preconditions (sec.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I may decide on the existence of the preconditions to any right to benefits: interruption of earnings and the minimum length of insurable employment (sec. 17 of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the specific points Agent I is empowered to decide when file appears complete and meets legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I authority: recognition of dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I is empowered to recognize a person as a dependent of the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of routine adjudication when no doubtful elements are revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I authority: disentitlement for failure to register with CMC (sec.55(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimant belongs to a class required by the UIC under sec. 55(7) to register with a CMC and has not submitted his CMC registration form with his application, the Agent I is empowered to declare him disentitled to benefit under that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent I retains responsibility for disallowance resulting from failure to comply with mandatory CMC registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I authority: establish earnings and allocate termination payments (regs.172–173)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimant has received earnings since becoming unemployed and does not dispute nature/amount, the Agent I can establish the amount and distribute it over the period (cf. reg. 172 and 173).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amounts affect entitlement and the date on which the claimant may begin receiving benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I limitation: generally only authorized to make favourable decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except under exceptional circumstances, an Agent I is only empowered to make decisions in favour of the claim; when items on the file justify denying the claim or disqualifying the claimant (sec. 41) or cast doubt on availability, Agent I must forward to Agent II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restricts Agent I's authority to avoid improper denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations always considered contentious (Agent II responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations are always 'contentious' and automatically come under Agent II: voluntary separation from former employment (disqualification under sec.41); dismissal for misconduct; applications referred by another District Office; applications for ordinary benefit subsequent to sickness/maternity benefit; applicants whose professions are in particular demand; applications by farmers, self-employed or part-time workers; cases where claimant wishes to antedate his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories raise special factual or legal issues (availability, definition of unemployment, circumstances of departure) requiring Agent II review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sickness and maternity adjudication limits for Agent I
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents I are not authorized to adjudicate claims for sickness benefits; they must forward those files to Agent II. Agents I may adjudicate maternity benefits only if application is submitted within the period during which benefits are payable (within the 15-week period beginning at the earliest 8 weeks before anticipated date of confinement; cf. sec. 30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside that period or for sickness claims, Agent II must decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate transfer for conflict of interest or undue pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Agent receiving a file who has a personal interest in the claim (relative/friend/obligation) or who is being pressured (threats/blackmail/bribery) must refrain from further action and ask the unit supervisor to transfer the claim (or transfer to the Regional Office in case of pressure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents biased decisions and protects integrity of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-phase processing by Agent I
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I processing has three phases: examination of the file (diversion of manifestly contentious claims), initial contact with claimant (telephone or interview, may divert claim), and the decision itself with notification and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under secs. 53(3) and 54(2) these operations should take place upon receiving a claim; in-person claims should be decided on the spot if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three levels of analysis in file examination (sec.54(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I must carry out a threefold analysis when examining an application: establish preconditions (sec.17), examine conditions for entitlement (sec.25), and identify elements which might result in disqualification (sec.41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent I may consult volume 4 of the UIC Manual for step-by-step operations and concise explanations of criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precondition criteria (insurable employment, qualifying weeks, interruption)
rubrics_metrics.description: On basis of application form and Record of Employment, Agent I must determine: whether insured has been employed in insurable employment; whether held such employment for at least 8 weeks during qualifying period (20 weeks for sickness/maternity); and whether there has been an interruption of earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Record is missing, agent queries claimant about steps taken and may draw up a temporary record if absence not due to claimant negligence (cf. reg.147).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer obligation to provide Record of Employment (reg.146) and practical noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer is required under reg.146 to provide the claimant with the Record of Employment within five days of termination; failure makes employer liable to a fine or imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice employers often fail to comply, especially small businesses, so agents must be prepared to use temporary records or claimant statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish average weekly earnings and allocate termination payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If preconditions fulfilled, Agent I establishes claimant's average weekly earnings and, if appropriate, amounts received upon termination of employment which are allocated to subsequent weeks at the average weekly rate (cf. regs.172 and 173).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These figures determine the amount of benefit payable and the date payments can begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maternity-specific evidence and timing (sec.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: For maternity benefits claimant must prove she held insurable employment for at least 10 weeks (or received ten weeks of benefits) during the 50th–30th weeks before the expected confinement; a medical certificate noting expected date is required; benefits period begins any time between 8 weeks before confinement and the week of confinement and lasts up to 15 weeks (sec.30(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications cannot be accepted without the medical certificate; Agent I may contact physician to establish expected date if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement conditions per sec.25 (incapable OR capable+available+unable to obtain employment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I examines whether applicant meets conditions for entitlement under sec.25: claimant must be either incapable of working due to illness/injury/quarantine, or (1) capable of working, (2) available for work, and (3) unable to obtain suitable employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent attempts to identify potential restrictions on ability to work, availability to look for work, or ability to find work (e.g., dependent children, profession demand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical evidence and Medical Yardsticks; overlapping benefits rules (sec.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: When illness period exceeds one week a medical certificate is required and Agent I uses 'Medical Yardsticks' to determine probable duration of inability; payments under workmen's compensation and group wage-loss indemnity interact with UI (sec.29 prohibits receiving workmen's comp and UI concurrently; group indemnity payments are deductible from UI benefits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent I examines these payments as part of entitlement analysis (cf. sec.29(3), sec.29(4), reg.172(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify possible disqualification under sec.41 (circumstances of separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I must identify elements suggesting disqualification under sec.41 (withholding benefits for 1–3 weeks) such as dismissal for misconduct or voluntary leaving without just cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record of Employment and application may conflict — Agent II should inquire further and contact employer; particularly sensitive dismissals (e.g., railway misconduct) must be referred to Regional Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-examination possible outcomes and forwarding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After examination Agent I will conclude: claim manifestly allowable (continue to favourable decision); manifestly unallowable or contentious (forward to Agent II or Regional Office); or doubtful (forward to Agent II) unless a simple explanation via interview will likely produce a favourable decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Agent I retains responsibility where disallowance results from absence of a precondition or failure to comply with mandatory CMC registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred contact modes and communication escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact with claimant normally takes the form of a telephone conversation, followed if necessary by a letter; in-person interviews are preferable when application submitted in person; mail used only as last resort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone priority loses advantage if unsuccessful attempts lead to unclarified applications; after 24 hours of unsuccessful phone attempts initiate correspondence; if written requests fail and claimant resides close by, ask him to appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification items to seek from claimant
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I should obtain missing application information (e.g., fuller details when 'Other' is checked for reason for leaving), gather further details for occupational groups (farmers, self-employed, part-time) via special questionnaires, clarify education/training status, dependent relationships, and reasons for any requested antedating of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claimant undertakes to deliver missing documents within agreed time the Agent will proceed at expiry; absence of a medical certificate makes a claim unallowable (sec.53 and reg.160(1)); absence of ROE may be made up by temporary record (reg.147(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Job referral duty (sec.106) and cooperation with CMC
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC shall assist in placing unemployed claimants by providing information, guidance and directing them to CMC; Agent I compares claimant's skills from CMC registration form with CMC list of vacancies and notifies CMC when suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMC arranges meeting with employer and notifies UIC of outcome, which Agent I reviews after one week to take into account in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for refusing job referral or offer
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant refuses to take advantage of job referral or refuses an offer of employment obtained through CMC, he will be liable to disqualification for 1–3 weeks (sec.40(1) and 43) or disentitlement (sec.25) and the claim becomes contentious, falling to Agent II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal triggers control sanctions and referral for further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I responsibility to explain and enforce active job search (sec.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I must ensure the claimant fulfils requirement of sec.55(8) by explaining the kind of search required: sector coverage, frequency of search attempts, and how attempts can be substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to search actively applies to all claimants except those receiving sickness, maternity or retirement benefits; Agent I's explanations are part of educational function of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Job Search Program and 'active job search statement' control function
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain claimants, especially whose skills are in particular demand locally, must submit at regular intervals an 'active job search statement' recording details of their search; although UIC states it helps placement, the immediate object is verification of availability and willingness to look for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is more an instrument of control than assistance; refusal to produce one may lead to disentitlement under sec.25(a) (deprivation of benefit until claimant changes attitude); refusal to comply with a written directive aimed at helping find work does not result in disqualification under sec.40(1)(c).
